note: First election of the rural district council (four district electoral divisions, two councillors each), polled 6 April 1899. At the first meeting Maynard Sinton and William Adams were co-opted and three additional councillors chosen (Banbridge Chronicle, 19 April 1899, p. 3); they are not filed. Returned unopposed. The only two nominated (Northern Whig, 18 March 1899, p. 7). The Banbridge Chronicle list of the new council names Walker for Ballyshiel; Mr. Harden took the chair at its first meeting.
